content.value_statement: Protected binaries can hide behavior behind anti-debugging, packing, virtualization, and obfuscation. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structure authorized analysis, document findings, and choose defensive next steps.
actual_capabilities: Explains common Windows and Linux anti-debugging checks.
Outlines VM detection, timing checks, and hardware fingerprinting indicators.
Describes obfuscation patterns such as control-flow flattening, opaque predicates, string encryption, and API hashing.
Summarizes packing and unpacking workflows for authorized malware or binary analysis.
Recommends common reverse engineering tools and documentation practices.
limitations: Does not verify legal authorization or engagement scope.
Does not replace expert reverse engineering or legal review.
Should not be used to bypass protections on software without permission.
Code samples require careful adaptation and isolated test environments.

use_cases.title: Triage Protected Malware
use_cases.description: Identify anti-debugging and packing indicators before deeper malware analysis.

use_cases.title: Plan Authorized Binary Testing
use_cases.description: Build a scoped workflow for reviewing software protection mechanisms during approved assessments.

use_cases.title: Teach Defensive Reverse Engineering
use_cases.description: Explain how obfuscation and anti-analysis controls affect investigation and reporting.

prompt_templates.title: Identify Protections
prompt_templates.prompt: I have authorization to analyze this binary. Help me identify likely anti-debugging, packing, and obfuscation indicators from my notes: [paste observations].

prompt_templates.title: Plan Safe Analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an authorized analysis plan for a protected Windows binary. Include setup, evidence handling, tools, and reporting steps.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Bypass Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Within this approved malware analysis lab, explain safe ways to study anti-debugging checks I found: [checks]. Focus on documentation and defensive conclusions.

prompt_templates.title: Build Technical Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn these reverse engineering notes into a professional report. Include protection summary, analysis method, impact, limitations, and defensive recommendations: [notes].

output_examples.input: Notes mention debugger checks, TracerPid checks, and timing checks.
output: Likely protection families: API anti-debugging, Linux tracing detection, and timing-based analysis detection.
Recommended report focus: observed behavior, analysis impact, lab controls, and defensive interpretation.

output_examples.input: A packed sample reaches a new entry point after debugger tracing.
output_examples.output: The output would summarize packer indicators, explain why the entry point matters, and list evidence needed for a defensible report.

output_examples.input: A training class needs a safe overview of obfuscation patterns.
output_examples.output: The skill can produce a concept-first lesson covering control flow, string hiding, API resolution, and analysis boundaries.

best_practices: Confirm authorization, scope, and legal constraints before using bypass guidance.
Work in isolated analysis environments and preserve evidence.
Share defensive conclusions instead of unnecessary step-by-step bypass details.
anti_patterns: Using the skill to bypass licensing, DRM, or access controls.
Running unknown binaries on production systems or personal devices.
Publishing detailed bypass steps without an authorized context.

faq.question: Is this skill only for malware analysis?
faq.answer: No. It also supports authorized penetration testing, CTF training, academic research, and analysis of software you are allowed to inspect.

faq.question: Can it prove that I am authorized?
faq.answer: No. You must confirm written authorization, scope, and legal constraints before using the guidance.

faq.question: Does it run reverse engineering tools?
faq.answer: No. It provides analysis guidance, checklists, and explanations. Tool execution remains under user control.

faq.question: Does it include bypass techniques?
faq.answer: Yes. The source material includes dual-use bypass guidance, so use it only in approved defensive or research contexts.

faq.question: Which platforms does it discuss?
faq.answer: It covers Windows and Linux anti-debugging, VM checks, obfuscation, packing, and virtualization-based protection.

faq.question: What should reports produced with it include?
faq.answer: Reports should include scope, observed protections, analysis method, evidence, impact, limitations, and defensive recommendations.
